messages:
Alex: FYI — regression observed in staging with speculative decoding when pairing Mistral draft models with Qwen production models. p95 latency +18% and acceptance rate down. Anyone digging in?

Maria: Yep, I started a short profile. Kernel selection is flipping to generic_attention on some input shapes and we're seeing KV cache eviction spikes around the same time.

Maria: Profile snippet:
```
seq_len=1024 model_pair=mistral->qwen
kernel_choice: fused_attn_v1 -> generic_attention
latencies_ms: fused=1.9 generic=4.1
kv_cache: hits=72.1% evictions=4.3/s
spec_accept=0.61
```

Cheng: Initial hypothesis: RoPE scaling + head/kv dim mismatches between families are triggering our kernel-picker fallbacks. The picker currently gates on dtype, seq_len, and a loose arch tag; it doesn't handle rope_scale or head_dim mismatches so it chooses a safe generic kernel. That increases latency and also causes more KV writes (different layout), hence evictions.

Sara: I repro'd locally. If I force rope_scale=1.0 during the handshake for the Mistral draft -> Qwen main pairing, the fused kernel stays selected and p95 returns to baseline. But forcing that globally could regress true Mistral-only runs.

Alex: Two obvious knobs: (A) tighten the handshake so model-pair negotiation includes rope_hint + preferred_kernel, and (B) normalize tokenizer output between draft and main to reduce token boundary mismatches that lower spec acceptance.

PerfBot: Canary after applying tokenizer normalization + kernel_hint on staging:
```
baseline p95=132ms
regressed p95=156ms
mitigated p95=134ms
spec_accept: 0.61 -> 0.79
GPU util: unchanged
```

Maria: Good signal. We need matrix coverage: Qwen (32h, 64h head variants) x Mistral/Mixtral drafts x contexts {1k,8k,32k}. Also test RoPE scaling factors (0.98,1.0,1.02) and kv_cache sizes to see eviction sensitivity. I'll add these to perf jobs.

Cheng: Another angle: speculative decoder acceptance threshold is tuned per model today. For cross-family pairing we could adapt threshold dynamically based on recent accept_rate & latency impact. Lower accept threshold -> more accepts -> less extra decode latency but higher risk of poor token quality. This is a cost/latency/quality tradeoff.

Sara: Action items I recorded: 1) add model-pair compatibility table + kernel_hint (owner: Maria, PR target: tomorrow), 2) expand perf test cases + include kv eviction metrics (owner: Maria), 3) RFC for dynamic acceptance gating based on family pairing (owner: Cheng). I'll open tickets and tag this thread.

Alex: @PerfBot can you attach the perf job IDs and link the canary dashboard in the ticket? Also please include the exact git patch that applied the kernel hint so we can roll forward/back easily. :thumbsup:

PerfBot: Done — canary job 2026-03-18-PR-421 attached to ticket INF-2187, dashboard https://perf.internal/redwood/canaries/2026-03-18-421. Patch: github.com/redwood/inference/commit/ba12c3f.

Maria: I'll start the expanded runs now. If anyone wants to pair on the tokenizer normalization logic later today ping me. :sparkles:

Cheng: I'll draft the RFC for adaptive acceptance thresholds and include a small sims harness to estimate latency vs acceptance vs quality.

Sara: Thanks all. Keeping this thread live for updates. :eyes:
